writeup.headline: Venture Global rates Hold: fast revenue growth and solid margins offset by heavy debt and negative free cash flow.
writeup.thesis: Venture Global scores 53, a Hold, with strong growth balanced against a weak balance sheet. TTM revenue growth of 100.7% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 47.6% year on year drive a growth score of 75, though growth slowed by 11.3 pp from the previous quarter. Profitability looks healthy at the operating level, with a 53.5% gross margin and a 37.6% operating margin, but the FCF margin is -41.2% as the company keeps spending heavily. That negative cash flow and cash covering only 0.07 of debt leave the balance sheet score at 4. Valuation scores 35: P/S of 2.2x and EV/EBIT of 12.0x are moderate in absolute terms, but the FCF yield is 23.4 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, and there is no comparison with its own history. The price trend is supportive, with the price 13.6% above its 200-day average.
key_risks: Heavy debt with negative free cash flow; cash covers only 0.07 of debt
Revenue growth is slowing, down 11.3 pp from the previous quarter
Repeated arbitration losses, including the Galp ruling against Calcasieu Pass, though damages are capped at $170M
Insider selling: the General Counsel sold roughly 790,000 shares and holds none directly
Most of the up-to-$17.2B power-island value is non-binding, so the data-center push may not materialize
what_would_change: A move to Buy needs 12 more points, most plausibly from free cash flow turning positive, which would lift balance sheet, quality and valuation scores
A drop to Sell would take a 9-point fall, for example from a further sharp slowdown in growth or the trend score weakening from 69
The Nov 10 Q3 report and any update to 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance could shift the growth and news scores
